title: Gap problem for 1-ball reconstruction threshold
statement_text: Determine the correct threshold $q^*(n)$ such that almost every $q$-colouring of the hypercube $Q_n$ is reconstructible from the multiset of its coloured 1-balls, narrowing the gap between the lower bound $q = \Omega(n)$ and the upper bound $q \geq n^{2+\varepsilon}$.
context_text: $Q_n$ is the $n$-dimensional hypercube on $\{0,1\}^n$, and the $r$-ball $B_r(v)$ is the subgraph induced by the vertices at distance at most $r$ from $v$; a $q$-colouring here is an arbitrary (not necessarily proper) assignment of $q$ colours to the vertices, and a random $q$-colouring colours each vertex independently and uniformly. Two colourings are equivalent if they differ by an automorphism of $Q_n$; they are $r$-locally equivalent if there is a bijection $f$ of $V(Q_n)$ such that the coloured $r$-ball around each $v$ in the first is isomorphic (as a coloured graph) to the coloured $r$-ball around $f(v)$ in the second. A colouring is $r$-distinguishable (reconstructible from the multiset of its coloured $r$-balls) if every $r$-locally equivalent colouring is equivalent to it. The authors prove that almost every $2$-colouring (indeed every random $(p,1-p)$-colouring with $p\ge n^{-1/4+\varepsilon}$) is $2$-distinguishable, and that a random $q$-colouring is $1$-distinguishable with high probability when $q\ge n^{2+K\log^{-1/2}n}$, in particular when $q\ge n^{2+\varepsilon}$. A counting argument shows that $\Omega(n)$ colours are necessary for reconstruction from $1$-balls. They expect $n^{1+o(1)}$ colours should suffice (neighbourhoods are already unique in that range), and believe but cannot prove that $1$-distinguishability with high probability is monotone in $q$.
notes: Stated informally in the introduction without a labelled environment: 'It is easy to show that Ω(n) colours are required for reconstructability, and it would be interesting to narrow the gap (see Sections 1.1 and 6 for further discussion).' Section 6, which reportedly contains further open questions, was not included in the provided text extract.
